ideas.title: Whiten item semantics before residual quantization
ideas.motivation: Dense item embeddings often devote much of their Euclidean distance to a few high-variance directions. Those directions can dominate nearest-code assignments even when lower-variance directions distinguish items that users substitute or compare, yielding IDs that waste code capacity on broad popularity/category axes.
ideas.novelty: Instead of changing the quantizer, codebook balance, hierarchy, or behavioral loss, use a fixed train-item covariance transform to change which embedding differences count equally during quantization. The transform is estimated once from the existing Stage 1 vectors and adds no learned per-step mechanism.
ideas.key_change: Compute a shrinkage-whitening linear map from training-item embeddings and feed transformed vectors to the otherwise unchanged RQ-VAE. Export SIDs from this model as usual; no item receives more than one global SID.
ideas.specification: Given train-only embeddings x_i in R^d, compute mu = mean_i(x_i), C = (1/N) sum_i (x_i-mu)(x_i-mu)^T, and eigendecomposition C=U diag(lambda) U^T. Set A=U diag((lambda+alpha*mean(lambda))^(-1/2)) U^T, with fixed alpha=0.05. Train the unchanged RQ-VAE on z_i=A(x_i-mu) with its existing reconstruction, commitment, and codebook losses; at export, encode each item's same z_i and write its ordinary single code tuple. Do not fit A using validation/test items or labels.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-time O(N*d^2 + d^3) CPU/GPU preprocessing (for N=24556 and the existing modest embedding dimension), then zero additional asymptotic work per training step beyond a stored transformed input tensor. Storage is O(N*d); at 24 steps/epoch and 3000 epochs the incremental per-step cost is effectively zero versus baseline RQ-VAE, so the full run remains baseline-feasible.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: On a fixed-seed Stage 2/Stage 3 comparison, covariance preconditioning improves test_R@10 over 0.06335, and the gain is accompanied by improved validation next-item ranking rather than merely lower reconstruction loss. Keep it only if the held-out test metric improves and train-only diagnostics show no pathological code collapse or large increase in SID collisions.
ideas.risks: Small eigenvalues may mostly represent noise, causing whitening to amplify unstable directions despite shrinkage; global covariance may erase useful broad semantic structure; and any Stage 3 gain may be within seed variance. Ensure preprocessing uses only train-item embeddings and hold all downstream training/evaluation settings fixed.

ideas.title: Temper residual magnitudes across quantization stages
ideas.motivation: In residual quantization, early-stage residuals can be much larger than later residuals, so reconstruction-driven training may over-optimize coarse semantic directions while fine code digits encode little useful distinction. This can make two items with different fine-grained needs share overly similar prefixes or leave later digits underused.
ideas.novelty: This changes the scale of the residual presented to each successive quantizer using a deterministic scalar schedule, rather than changing geometry, branching, assignment balancing, or adding a behavior-derived objective. It keeps the same codebooks, number of stages, and global item-to-tuple assignment.
ideas.key_change: Normalize the residual entering each later stage by a fixed stage-specific scalar, while accumulating the correspondingly rescaled quantized contribution, so all stages operate on comparable residual scales without adding trainable parameters.
ideas.specification: For encoder output h_i and K residual codebooks, initialize r_i^(0)=h_i. For stage l, compute s_l = sqrt(mean_train(||r_i^(l)||_2^2)/d) once from a short baseline warm-up checkpoint (stop-gradient, train items only), then quantize u_i^(l)=r_i^(l)/max(s_l,1e-6) with the existing nearest-code rule. Set q_i^(l)=s_l * e_{a_i^l}^{(l)}, r_i^(l+1)=r_i^(l)-q_i^(l), and reconstruct h-hat_i=sum_l q_i^(l). Freeze s_l for the subsequent training run; use the same scales at export. Compare against an identical baseline warm-up and exclude held-out items from scale estimation.
ideas.cost_estimate: The per-step change is K scalar divisions/multiplications on existing tensors and no additional pairwise distances or optimizer state: O(batch*d*K) elementwise work, expected well below 1% of baseline RQ-VAE step time. Scale estimation is one train-item pass after warm-up. At 24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, and 3000 epochs this remains feasible on one GPU.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The fixed scales make later-stage code usage and per-stage residual-energy reduction less degenerate, and this translates into higher validation and test next-item R@10 than the untempered model (targeting improvement over test_R@10 0.06335). If only code utilization changes without a repeatable ranking gain, discard the idea.
ideas.risks: Stage scales estimated from an early checkpoint may be stale; scaling may interact badly with the commitment/codebook loss magnitudes; and normalizing a stage could encourage fine digits to encode noise. Use a fixed scale protocol decided before the run, log per-stage residual and usage statistics, and evaluate with identical Stage 3 settings.
